newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: French retailer Auchan opens 'euro' supermarket.
newsitem.headline: French retailer Auchan opens 'euro' supermarket.

text.p: French retailer Groupe Auchan on Monday opened a supermarket in the heart of the European district in Luxembourg City where customers can pay with the euro, Europe's future single currency.
Buyers, estimated at a daily 5,000 to 10,000, are expected to not come just from the Kirchberg district which houses European Union buildings and large office blocks.

The 12,000 square-metre shop, which employs 750 staff from 22 nations speaking at least French, German and Luxembourgois, aims to lure shoppers away from border towns in France, Germany and Belgium, Auchan said.

As a result the market will accept payment in French francs and German marks. With Belgium and Luxembourg in a monetary union for some 70 years, their currencies will raise the number of monies accepted by the shop to five.

One of the supermarket's attractions to foreign buyers is the comparatively low rate of value-added tax in Luxembourg, Auchan said. The top VAT rate there is 15 percent compared to for instance 21 percent in Belgium.

Auchan management said at the opening government opposition to Sunday trading meant the loss of 150 potential jobs. To offset the curb, the shop intended to stretch Saturday opening hours beyond the current local close at 1800 local (1700 GMT).
Auchan, with sales of 124 billion French francs ($24.2 billion) the world's ninth largest supermarket group, plans to open further shops in Hungary, Argentina and Thailand.
